case_studies.title: AgentBrew: Lifelong Knowledge Brewing from Strong Teachers to Weak LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Deploying LLM agents typically requires a compact test-time student, even if a stronger teacher is available during training. We study knowledge brewing: distilling a teacher's interactive experience into a persistent external memory for the student. Crucially, this requires no weight updates, expert demonstrations, ground-truth labels, or test-time teacher access. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of deploying large language model (LLM) agents that require a lot of training data and computational power, by creating a system that can distill knowledge from a stronger teacher into a weaker student agent. The authors built a system called AgentBrew that can transfer knowledge from a teacher to a student agent without requiring weight updates or test-time teacher access. The result is a more efficient and effective way to train LLM agents.

case_studies.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
case_studies.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) on open-ended tasks compresses an LLM's rubric-based evaluation into a scalar reward, discarding rich textual feedback and conflating responses with distinct quality profiles. We propose Experiential Learning (EL), which repurposes the feedback model from an LLM-as-a-Judge into an LLM-as-a-Coach. case_studies.abstract: Rubric-based RL has recently shown promise in improving LLMs on open-ended tasks.
